text: A non-VLAN-aware PC should belong to VLAN 20 on a Cisco switch. Which interface command assigns an already configured access port to that VLAN?
distractors: switchport trunk native vlan 20
ip default-gateway 20
channel-group 20 mode active
explanation: An access port's data-VLAN membership is set with switchport access vlan 20. A trunk native VLAN setting applies to trunk behavior, not the requested access membership. The port should operate in access mode and VLAN 20 must exist.

text: An 802.1Q trunk uses its default native-VLAN tagging behavior, and native VLAN tagging has not been enabled. How is ordinary native-VLAN traffic transmitted on that trunk?
distractors: With two nested 802.1Q tags
Only as an IP multicast packet
With a VLAN tag whose value is always zero
explanation: Under the stated default behavior, native-VLAN frames are sent untagged on an 802.1Q trunk. Other carried VLANs are tagged. Explicit native-VLAN tagging configuration can change this behavior, so the question's configuration assumptions matter.

text: VLAN 20 exists on both switches and its access ports work locally. Their trunk is up, but its allowed list contains only VLAN 10. What change directly addresses VLAN 20's interswitch failure?
correct: Add VLAN 20 to the trunk's allowed VLAN list on the relevant ends
distractors: Change VLAN 20's hosts to the VLAN 10 subnet while leaving the ports unchanged
Increase the switch's MAC aging timer
Enable PortFast on every trunk to override the allowed list
explanation: A trunk only carries VLANs permitted by its allowed list, subject to other forwarding conditions. VLAN 20 must be allowed along the path. Host address changes and MAC timers do not repair VLAN filtering, and PortFast does not override an allowed list.

text: Two otherwise compatible switch ports are being bundled with LACP. One side uses active mode. Which peer mode can negotiate an EtherChannel with it?
distractors: PAgP auto mode without LACP
LACP passive on both sides after changing the active side to passive
A shutdown interface
explanation: LACP active initiates negotiation and passive responds, so active/passive can form a bundle when the remaining parameters match. Passive/passive does not initiate negotiation. PAgP uses a different protocol, and an administratively down link cannot negotiate.

text: For VLAN 10, two switches have the same configured bridge priority and VLAN system-ID extension. Switch A has MAC 0011.2233.4400 and switch B has MAC 0011.2233.5500. Which switch becomes the root bridge, assuming no lower bridge ID exists?
correct: Switch A, because its MAC portion makes its bridge ID lower
distractors: Switch B, because the larger MAC indicates a newer switch
The switch with the highest-numbered access port
Neither, because equal priorities prevent an election
explanation: Spanning tree elects the lowest bridge ID. When priority and the VLAN system-ID extension are equal, the lower MAC address breaks the tie. 0011.2233.4400 is lower than 0011.2233.5500; port numbering and device age do not select the root.

text: An endpoint-facing port has PortFast and BPDU guard enabled. A small switch is connected and sends a BPDU. What is the expected BPDU guard response?
correct: Place the protected port into an error-disabled state
distractors: Automatically make the new switch the root bridge
Convert the port to a routed interface
Ignore all BPDUs indefinitely while continuing to forward
explanation: BPDU guard protects an edge port from unexpected BPDUs by error-disabling it. PortFast alone accelerates transition to forwarding; it does not authorize attaching another spanning-tree participant. Investigate the cause before recovering the port.

text: A network uses switches from several vendors. Which standards-based protocol can report directly connected neighbor and port information when supported and enabled on those devices?
distractors: OSPF
NTP
DHCP relay
explanation: LLDP is a vendor-neutral link-layer discovery protocol that advertises local device and port information. OSPF exchanges routing information, NTP synchronizes clocks, and DHCP relay forwards address-configuration messages. Neighbor discovery must be enabled on the relevant links.

text: An administrator needs encrypted remote CLI access to a switch across an IP network. Which management method is appropriate?
distractors: Telnet
An unencrypted HTTP-only management session
CDP neighbor advertisements
explanation: SSH encrypts the remote terminal session and supports authenticated access. Telnet does not provide that encryption. HTTP-only access is also unencrypted, and CDP is a discovery mechanism, not an interactive CLI session. Encryption does not replace access-control configuration.

text: An AP joins a wireless LAN controller using CAPWAP. The WLAN is explicitly configured for central switching. Where is its client data normally tunneled for forwarding?
distractors: Directly to every other AP without reaching the controller
To a DNS server as the wireless data-plane gateway
To the client device's DHCP lease database
explanation: In the stated centrally switched design, the AP tunnels client data to the controller, which forwards it onto the configured network. Other supported modes can switch client data locally, so controller management alone would not establish this data path.

text: A controller-managed SSID should place clients in the guest network. Clients associate successfully but receive addresses from the staff subnet. Which WLAN setting should be checked first?
correct: The WLAN's interface or VLAN mapping
distractors: The text of the AP's physical inventory label
The controller's preferred syslog severity
The switch's MAC aging timer
explanation: The WLAN-to-interface or VLAN mapping determines the network into which client traffic is placed in the described design. Association success does not prove that this mapping is correct. DHCP configuration should also be checked after confirming that client traffic reaches the intended guest network.
